mediaplanr — Implementation Plan (Nov 2026, rev 2)

Source: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md

Hand-off plan for Claude Code. Read this whole file, then Roadmap.md and vignette("plan_concepts"), before writing code. The Roadmap’s “Decided” sections are binding unless this plan explicitly amends them.

Goal of this run: make mediaplanr the plan-state and action layer of an agentic media planner: an agent can inspect a plan compactly, act on it only through validated ops, never violate commercial commitments, be scored by mrmopt at the right grain, check itself against the same constraints the optimizer uses, and leave an auditable record of what it changed and why.

Rev 2 adds: spend bounds (commitments), structured rationale, describe_plan(), a model-to-plan grain map, and a shared constraint object.

0. Why this plan exists

The package was stress-tested against a real agency national digital plan (Q4 2026, ~266 monthly line items across streaming, programmatic and YouTube; 27 workbook tabs), then reviewed for fitness as an agent’s substrate.

Plan-modelling findings:

  • Validated: the flat table at a configurable grain. Every flowchart, finance pivot and QA tab in the workbook is a roll_up() + calendarize() view of one long table.
  • Most common real edit is a zero-sum transfer (“move $X from partner A in Feb to partner B in Feb”). The workbook keeps a 230-row change log of exactly these. Today that is two delta ops whose pairing is lost.
  • Much of the spend is not movable. Upfront direct-IO commitments, partner minimums and already-spent months are fixed. Nothing in the model says so.
  • Approvals form a dated chain (five approved versions in one year). The package cannot say which approved version is current, and @revision resets to 1 on every derivation — the opposite of what a planner means by “Rev 2”.
  • The real “topline” is a budget envelope, not a subplan: signed channel × quarter authorizations checked with tolerated variance.
  • Spend has two bases (media net vs. client net incl. fees); nothing declares which one a plan holds.
  • Credit rows are negative. The non-negative validator is correct — credits are billing reconciliation, not intent — but the docs must say so.

Agent-readiness findings:

  • Strong already: value semantics, validator on every construction, ops as data, errors that list alternatives, lineage + status. An agent cannot corrupt a plan, and every proposal is an inspectable scenario.
  • Missing: (1) commitments the edit path respects; (2) a compact, bounded plan summary for the agent’s context; (3) a deterministic map from plan line items to mrmopt response models; (4) one constraint object both the agent’s self-check and the optimizer read; (5) structured rationale on each proposal.
  • API style: consumers are LLM agents (JSON tool calls, or generated R). Tidy-eval / dplyr methods / per-step pipe verbs are rejected (Phase 0 records why). Op constructors + one JSON Schema are the chosen interface.

Responsibility split (record in the Roadmap, Phase 0): mediaplanr = plan state, legal actions, constraints, checks, history. mrmopt = scoring and optimization. The app = the agent loop and the human approval gate.

1. Standing rules (apply to every phase)

  • Read the existing code before changing it. Follow its conventions; do not restyle untouched code.
  • Explicit S7:: namespacing. No new hard dependencies (current Imports: S7, jsonlite, stats, utils — keep it that way).
  • Every copy goes through .copy_plan(). New slots are carried by default; any constructor that must reset a slot does so explicitly and has a test proving it.
  • Nothing derived is stored; nothing from Sys.Date(). If a value can change without the plan changing, it is a function argument or a projection, never a slot.
  • Errors name the fix. Mistyped targets error with alternatives. Pairing checks (plan vs. external artifact: decomp, budget, models, constraints) warn and return a table; structural problems error.
  • No guessing: where intent is ambiguous, error naming the explicit form.
  • Everything an agent receives or sends is JSON-representable: plain lists and data frames, ISO dates, no closures, no environments.
  • Tests written alongside code (testthat 3e). Run devtools::test() after every phase and devtools::check() at the end of every phase; both clean before moving on. One commit per phase (or per sub-step if large), message prefixed with the phase number.
  • New settable slots are serialized automatically via .settable_props(); verify the JSON round-trip for each one. Bump .plan_schema_version to 4 exactly once (first phase that adds a slot, Phase 4) and keep all new fields optional on read so v1–v3 files still load.
  • Reserved @data columns (like flight_id, pacing, unit_type) travel through JSON with @data; confirm round-trip for any new one.
  • Use synthetic fixtures only. No client names anywhere — this repo is public.
  • describe_plan() (Phase 5) is the agent’s view of a plan: every later phase that adds a plan fact adds it there too, with a test.

2. Decisions Ben confirms before the run

Defaults below are what to implement if unchanged.

# Decision Default
D1 @revision Remove the slot; revision becomes a lineage projection (Phase 6).
D2 transfer into a destination whose current spend is 0 Spread evenly by in-market days across matched rows (same rule as an even flight).
D3 Provenance for data-frame / named-vector edits Store the allocation as given, so every derivation is replayable.
D4 @spend_basis vocabulary Free text, documented common values; strict equality where plans combine.
D5 Group ops (delta, total, transfer) touching bounded rows Bounds-aware: distribute proportionally across rows with headroom, clipping at bounds (water-filling); error only if infeasible. Single-row ops (set, scale, delta_each) that breach a bound error.
D6 Granularity of commitments Row-level bounds in @data (per line item per period). Flight- or line-total commitments (“$300K upfront, phasing flexible”) are group constraints in Phase 10.
D7 Release split 0.2.0 after Phase 8; 0.3.0 after Phase 10.

Release 0.2.0 — the agent can act safely

Phase 0 — Roadmap & doc housekeeping (docs only)

  1. Roadmap.md
    • Replace the stray, indented ## Tydification stub with an “API style — decided” section:
      • In: plan-first arguments, pure functions returning the same class, standard evaluation, op_*() constructors, one JSON Schema.
      • Out, with reasons: dplyr generics on MediaPlan (bypass validation, units identity, subplan locks, flight identity, spend bounds); tidy-eval / bare column names (not JSON-serializable, unusable by tool-calling agents); per-step mutating pipe verbs (each step would mint a lineage generation — one intent must be one scenario). Read-only projections may be piped freely.
    • Add an “Agentic planner: responsibility split” section (text in §0 above), and the agent loop it supports: describe → propose ops → validate → score (mrmopt, via the model map) → check constraints → record rationale → human approves.
    • SubPlans: add a “Status: held” note — built and tested at one level; no further investment (depth, staleness detection) and not exposed in the app until a real multi-owner engagement needs it. Point to check_budget() (Phase 8) as the common envelope case.
    • Move items to “Already grown” as phases land.
  2. vignette("plan_concepts"): fix “imports nothing but S7” (jsonlite, stats, utils are imported). Add a short “Credits are not intent” subsection: negative billing adjustments stay out of @data; net them into the line’s planned spend only if they change planned media, otherwise keep them in a separate adjustments table outside the plan.

Done when: devtools::check() clean, vignettes build.

Phase 1 — Op registry, op_*() constructors, plan_ops_schema()

Pure refactor + additions; no behavior change to existing ops.

  1. Registry. In R/verbs.R (or new R/ops.R, add to Collate), define .op_registry: one entry per op key with its family (value/structural), fields, field types, required/optional, and one-line description. Derive .value_ops, .structural_ops, .op_keys, and the allowed-field check in .apply_op() from it, so there is one source of truth.
  2. Constructors (exported, documented, examples): op_set(), op_scale(), op_delta(), op_delta_each(), op_total(), op_add(), op_drop(), op_shift(), op_restage() (and op_transfer() in Phase 2).
    • Each returns a plain list identical to the hand-written op (no class attribute), so constructor-built, hand-built and JSON-parsed ops are interchangeable.
    • Validate plan-independent arguments at construction (types, lengths, during shape, ISO date strings parse). Plan-dependent validation stays in .apply_op().
    • Signature pattern: op_scale(by, target = NULL, during = NULL).
  3. plan_ops_schema(plan = NULL, as_json = FALSE) → JSON Schema for the edits array, built from the registry (oneOf over op shapes).
    • With plan supplied, narrow target property names to line_item_grain(plan) and their values to grain_values() enums, and the time format to the plan’s basis. This is the agent-facing contract.
  4. Update ?build_scenario examples to show constructors alongside raw lists.

Tests: every constructor identical() to its raw-list equivalent; invalid args error at construction; registry-derived .op_keys equals the old constant; schema validates a corpus of known-good ops and rejects known-bad ones (a small recursive checker in the test helper — no new dependency); plan-aware schema enumerates the fixture’s grain values.

Phase 2 — transfer op

Shape (constructor op_transfer(amount, from, to, during = NULL, from_during = NULL, to_during = NULL)):

list(transfer = 37419,
     from = list(partner = "DSP A"),
     to   = list(tactic  = "Regional"),
     during = list(from = "2026-10-01", to = "2026-10-31"))

Semantics: - amount > 0, single number. from / to are targets (same rules as target). transfer takes no target. - during applies to both sides; from_during / to_during override per side. Supplying during and a per-side override for the same side errors. - Source side behaves like delta = -amount; destination like delta = +amount when its current sum > 0; when it is 0, apply D2 (even by in-market days across matched rows, using the flights’ day-span helper). Document on ?op_transfer. - Implement distribution through one internal helper (e.g. .distribute(ps, change, weights, lower, upper)) used by delta, total and transfer. In this phase lower = 0, upper = Inf; Phase 3 feeds it real bounds. This keeps D5 a one-place change. - Source and destination row sets must be disjoint → else error. - Destination matching no rows → error naming add (introduce the line item first, in the same edits list). - Subplan-backed rows on either side → the existing .stop_if_backed() error. - Post-condition: total planned spend unchanged within cent tolerance (internal assertion — a failure is a bug). - Units and pacing re-derive in .apply_edits() already — verify, do not duplicate.

Tests: budget neutrality across grains; proportional source; zero-destination spread (weekly with ragged flight, daily, monthly); per-side windows; overlap error; below-zero error; no-match destination error; subplan lock; units follow at held rate; flight stays "even" under proportional moves; compare_scenarios(level = "flight") unaffected. Replace the “Move 10 from TV to Search” two-delta example with op_transfer().

Phase 3 — Spend bounds (commitments)

Make “this money cannot move” a fact in the plan that every edit respects.

  1. Reserved optional @data columns min_spend and max_spend (numeric, NA = unbounded). Authored at import (media_plan_from_df(), media_plan_from_flights() pass them through) or via op_add(). Nothing else is stored.
    • Validator: 0 <= min_spend <= planned_spend <= max_spend wherever bounds are present (cent tolerance). Negative or inverted bounds error.
  2. Commitment is derived, not stored. Internal .commitment() labels each row: "committed" (min == max == spend), "floor" (min > 0), "capped" (finite max), "flexible" (none). Surfaced in line_item_summary() (committed spend / flexible headroom per line) and later in describe_plan().
  3. Edit enforcement (D5):
    • .distribute() water-fills: allocate the change proportionally across matched rows, clip any row at its bound, redistribute the remainder over rows with headroom, repeat. If the change cannot be absorbed, error naming the binding rows and the absorbable amount.
    • set, scale, delta_each: compute, then error if any matched row would breach its bound — name the rows and their bounds.
    • drop of a row with min_spend > 0 errors (a floor cannot be dropped; the fix is to lower the floor via a data-frame edit that also supplies bounds — see 5).
    • shift / restage: bounds move with their rows; restaging a committed flight errors unless the flight’s per-row bounds map 1:1.
    • Data-frame allocation edits (optimizer output) that breach a bound error; the optimizer must be given the bounds (Phase 10 makes that one object).
  4. Interactions: even-pacing snapping must not push a row past a bound (skip snapping rows whose bound binds; test it). roll_up() sums min_spend (NA treated as 0) and sums max_spend (NA if any NA). calendarize() splits bounds by the same day weights as spend. Subplan rollups carry summed bounds. compare_scenarios() unaffected.
  5. Changing a bound is an explicit act, never a side effect of a spend op. Add op rebound (op_rebound(target, min = , max = , during = )) to set bounds on matched rows; it changes no spend, and errors if the new bounds exclude current spend. Register it in the Phase 1 registry/schema.

Tests: validator matrix; water-fill (partial absorption, full binding, infeasible error message); each op family against committed, floor, capped rows; snapping near a bound; roll_up/calendarize of bounds; JSON round-trip of bound columns; transfer that must route around committed rows; rebound legality.

Phase 4 — Provenance: @edits, @rationale, edit_log()

  1. New settable slot @edits (S7::class_list, default list()): the edits that produced this plan from @parent_id, in canonical form:
    • op form → list(form = "ops", ops = <normalized op list>) (dates as ISO strings; single op wrapped into a list).
    • data frame / named vector → per D3: list(form = "allocation", data = <grain cols + planned_spend df>).
  2. New settable slot @rationale (S7::class_list, default list()): structured reasons for a derivation, alongside the human headline in @objective. Allowed keys (validator rejects others): author ("human" / "agent" / "optimizer"), goal (string), constraints_id (string, Phase 10 id), forecast (named list of numeric KPIs supplied by the caller — the package never computes them), notes (string). Set via a rationale = argument on build_scenario().
  3. Both are set by build_scenario(). Explicit resets to list(): roots (media_plan_from_df(), _from_flights()) and roll_up(). revise() and attach_subplan() / detach_subplan() carry them (same id); revise() may set rationale (it describes the plan, not its spend).
  4. Validator: @edits empty or canonical; non-empty @edits requires non-empty @parent_id.
  5. Serialization (bump schema to 4 here): include both; reader restores structure (parse these subtrees with simplifyVector = FALSE or coerce explicitly; length-1 target vectors must stay vectors).
  6. edit_log(set) → one row per op across the set, in lineage order: scenario, parent, author, op, from (target label via the .cell_label() labeller), to, amount, window, objective. Transfers fill both sides; one-sided ops fill one; allocations report one row (op = "allocation", amount = net change).
  7. Replay property: internal .replay(parent, edits); .replay(parent, child@edits) reproduces child@data exactly.

Tests: provenance set/reset matrix across every constructor and verb; replay property over all op forms incl. transfer and rebound; rationale key validation; JSON round-trip incl. multi-value targets and moments with @tz; edit_log() on a three-generation chain with mixed authors.

Phase 5 — describe_plan(plan, top_n = 10)

The agent’s compact, stable view of a plan. Returns a plain named list, JSON-ready, bounded in size regardless of plan size:

  • identity: name, nickname, id (short), parent_id, status, objective, rationale$author
  • shape: grain (coarsest-first), time_col, time_basis, flight window, number of line items and rows, is_topline + subplan cells
  • money: total spend; spend by the coarsest grain column; for each finer column, the top_n values by spend plus an other bucket
  • commitments: committed / floor-locked / flexible spend and the number of bounded line items; total headroom (flexible + above-floor)
  • units: totals by unit_type, blended rate per type
  • time: spend by calendar month (via calendarize())
  • targetable: the grain values an op may target (truncated to top_n per column with a count of the rest — the full list comes from plan_ops_schema(plan))

Later phases append fields (approval, basis, budget, model coverage, constraints). Optional args are added as those phases land: describe_plan(plan, budget = NULL, models = NULL, constraints = NULL).

Tests: structure snapshot on fixtures (expect_snapshot of the JSON); size bound on a synthetic 5,000-row plan (serialized length under a fixed budget); every number reconciles to @data.

Phase 6 — Approvals: @approved_on, revision as projection, current approved

  1. @revision removal (D1). Remove the slot; grep all uses (~38 in R/, plus print header, subplan_map(), lineage(), serialize, tests) and update. revise(revision = ) → error naming lineage(). v2/v3 files carrying revision load with it ignored. Note in the Roadmap that the consuming app may reference @revision (set_status_tool); do not edit the app here.
  2. @approved_on (S7::class_Date, default length-0 = unset). Validator: length 0 or 1; non-empty only when @status == "approved". revise() clears it automatically when status leaves “approved”; the validator is the backstop. Settable via revise(status = "approved", approved_on = "2026-10-29") (Date or ISO). Optional even when approved — never defaulted from Sys.Date(). build_scenario() and roll_up() reset it. Printed in the header.
  3. lineage(set) gains approved_on; revision = ordinal among approved plans on the root → self path (NA if not approved); current = approved with no approved descendant in the set.
  4. current_approved(set) → name(s) flagged current. None → character(0) with a message; several (parallel branches) → all, with a warning. Never break ties by date.
  5. compare_scenarios(set, level, against = c("base", "parent", "current_approved")) — default preserves behavior; "current_approved" errors unless exactly one exists.
  6. describe_plan() adds approved_on.

Tests: five-version approval chain with a rejected branch; current detection; parallel-approved warning; status change clears date; derived scenarios never inherit it; against options reconcile with lineage(); old JSON with revision loads.

Phase 7 — @spend_basis

  1. Settable character scalar, default "" (undeclared). Free text (D4); document common values "media_net", "client_net", "gross".
  2. Set at construction (media_plan_from_df(..., spend_basis = ); _from_flights() forwards) or via revise() (a declaration correction, never a conversion — say so).
  3. Carried by build_scenario() and roll_up() (test it).
  4. Strict equality where plans combine: ScenarioSet validator and attach_subplan() error on mismatch, naming revise(spend_basis = ).
  5. Header + describe_plan() show it. Serialized (schema 4).

Out of scope: fee schedules or basis conversion (record in Roadmap: belongs in the caller or a companion package).

Phase 8 — check_budget(plan, budget, tolerance = 0.5)

The envelope check, by analogy with check_coverage().

  • budget: data frame with zero or more columns from line_item_grain(plan), plus from, to (Date or ISO), and amount. Rows may overlap. Unknown columns error with alternatives.
  • Planned spend per budget row = sum of the plan’s spend inside [from, to] for matching grain values, via calendarize(plan, "day") (works for every basis). Budget values absent from the plan → planned 0 (reported).
  • Returns budget rows plus planned, variance = planned - amount, variance_pct. Warns listing rows with abs(variance) > tolerance.
  • Works unchanged on toplines.
  • Help pages for check_budget() and attach_subplan() contrast them: an envelope is a target checked with tolerance; a subplan is ownership with equality.
  • describe_plan(budget = ) adds a compact variance summary.

Tests: quarterly channel envelope vs. a monthly plan; month boundary mid-week on a weekly plan; whole-plan envelope; missing grain value; tolerance edge; instant-basis plan.

Then release 0.2.0 (see Phase 11 checklist, applied to Phases 0–8).

Release 0.3.0 — the agent can be scored and checked

Phase 9 — Model-to-plan grain map: model_map(), spend_by_model()

mrmopt models are fitted at a grain that may differ from the plan’s — and may be mixed (some channel-level, some partner-level). Make the mapping explicit and deterministic.

  • models: data frame, one row per fitted response model, columns a subset of line_item_grain(plan) plus model_id. A coarser model leaves finer columns NA (e.g. channel = "YouTube", partner = NA). Unknown columns error with alternatives. Duplicate keys error.
  • model_map(plan, models) → one row per plan line item: grain columns, model_id, match_level (the columns matched), spend. Resolution: most specific matching model wins; two equally specific matches → error naming both; no match → model_id = NA. Warns with unmodeled spend and its share (pairing check: plan and models are each valid).
  • spend_by_model(plan, models, basis = "week") → long data frame model_id × period × planned_spend (and units where single-typed): the exact input a response-model forecast needs. Unmapped spend is returned under model_id = NA, never dropped silently. Uses calendarize() then aggregation over the map.
  • Pure data frames in and out; no dependency on mrmopt. Document the hand-off in the vignette with an eval = FALSE mrmopt example.
  • describe_plan(models = ) adds coverage: modeled share and the top unmodeled line items.

Tests: exact-grain match; mixed-grain resolution; ambiguity error; unmodeled warning and share; NA bucket retained; totals reconcile to the plan for every basis; flighted and instant plans.

Phase 10 — Shared constraint object: plan_constraints(), check_constraints()

One definition of “allowed” that the agent’s self-check (here) and the optimizer (mrmopt, later) both read.

  1. PlanConstraints S7 class (thin): @id, @name, and @rules, a data frame with one row per rule:
    • target (list-column of grain targets; empty = whole plan), during (optional from / to),
    • type ∈ min_spend, max_spend, min_share, max_share, max_change_abs, max_change_pct, fixed_total (covers D6’s flight-level commitments: total fixed, phasing free),
    • value (numeric), note. Validator: known types, shares in [0, 1], max_change_* non-negative, targets well-formed. Row-level bounds stay in @data (Phase 3); this object holds group rules.
  2. Constructors: plan_constraints(rules, name) from a data frame, plus rule_*() helpers mirroring the op-constructor pattern (rule_min_share(target, value, during) …). JSON round-trip via plan_to_json() / plan_from_json() (add an object tag). constraints_schema() for agents, built like plan_ops_schema().
  3. check_constraints(plan, constraints, reference = NULL) → one row per rule: actual, limit, slack, ok. Share rules are relative to the whole plan within the same during window. max_change_* rules need reference (normally the parent or current approved plan) and error naming the argument if it is missing. Also reports row-level bound violations (should be none — validator — but keep the report complete). Warns on any violation; never errors on a violation.
  4. Targets validated against the plan exactly as op targets are (typos error with alternatives).
  5. rationale$constraints_id (Phase 4) references @id; describe_plan(constraints = ) adds a pass/fail summary with the binding rules.
  6. Roadmap: add “mrmopt reads PlanConstraints” as the next cross-package step; do not modify mrmopt in this run.

Tests: each rule type pass/fail/edge; share within windows; change rules against a reference; missing-reference error; JSON round-trip; schema validates good rules and rejects bad; constraints checked on a scenario built by transfers that respect row bounds but break a share rule.

Phase 11 — Fixture, docs, finish (run at each release boundary)

  1. fix_agency_plan() in tests/testthat/helper-fixtures.R (add in Phase 2, extend as phases land): synthetic, monthly, grain channel + partner + campaign + tactic, impressions with CPM rates; one zero-spend line; one added-value line (tiny rate); committed upfront rows (min_spend == max_spend); a partner with a floor; three channels, two quarters. Companion fix_agency_models() (mixed-grain) and fix_agency_constraints().
  2. vignette("getting_started"): end-to-end — import the agency fixture, approve it, two transfers that route around commitments in one scenario, edit_log(), check_budget(), compare_scenarios(against = "current_approved"). In 0.3.0 add model_map() / spend_by_model() and check_constraints().
  3. New vignette("agentic_planning") (0.3.0): the loop from Phase 0 with real calls — describe_plan() → ops validated against plan_ops_schema(plan) → build_scenario(rationale = ) → spend_by_model() (mrmopt call eval = FALSE) → check_constraints() → revise(status = "to review"). Explain what the agent may and may not do, and why commitments live in the plan.
  4. vignette("plan_concepts"): transfers & provenance; commitments as bounds (and why the label is derived); approvals as a lineage projection; spend basis.
  5. Roadmap.md: move shipped items to “Already grown”; keep in “Not yet built”: mrmopt consuming PlanConstraints; a spreadsheet importer as a companion package (mediaplanr.io: declarative column map + regex rules → MediaPlan + lint report; keeps readxl out of this package).
  6. NEWS.md; version bump (0.2.0, then 0.3.0); pkgdown reference index for new exports (op_*, plan_ops_schema, edit_log, describe_plan, current_approved, check_budget, model_map, spend_by_model, PlanConstraints, plan_constraints, rule_*, constraints_schema, check_constraints).
  7. Final devtools::check() clean.

Out of scope for this run

Forecasting, optimization, fee/basis conversion, an Excel importer, geo taxonomies, external ID joins, any change to mediaplanr-mvp-app or mrmopt, the agent loop itself, and further subplan work.
